wy_1_blooming_rose.blurb: Blooming Rose is a sport wall in the OK Corral section of the high-plateau Wild Iris area outside Lander, at roughly 8,900 feet. It shares its cliff line with Claim Jumper and Saddle Tramp, and it is a good stop for climbers who want plenty of mid-grade pulling. About twenty-two climbs are recorded here, nearly all bolted, with a single boulder problem. Grades start around 5.7 and run up to the low 5.13s, but the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with 5.11 the most common. Expect other parties on the wall, and reach it by following any of the trails that branch off the main dirt road.
wy_1_blooming_rose.approach: Any of the trails leaving the main dirt road leads to the wall.

wy_school_the.blurb: The School is the gentlest of the crags on the south side of Sinks Canyon near Lander, in the Shady Side group. It is a compact sport area with about twenty-two bolted lines, running from an easy 5.6 up to the low 5.13s, though the weight of the grades sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. The climbing swings from low-angle slab to steep roofs, with a mix of jugs, pockets and cracks, and there are comfortable ledges at the base. The wall catches morning shade and has tree cover, and the whole Shady Side group stays cool through most of the day. Because it is the most approachable wall here, it is often busy.

wy_second_wind_wall.blurb: Second Wind Wall is a newer sport wall in Piney Creek Canyon, in the Eastern Big Horns of Wyoming. It sits a short scramble above the Trailside Wall, well up the slope from the creek trail, so it feels more private than the walls beside the water. It holds about twenty-two climbs, nearly all of them bolted and two on trad gear, with grades from 5.6 to the low 5.12s and the greatest number in the 5.10 to 5.12 band. The face gets more sun than its neighbors, which keeps the rock clean and lets it be climbed earlier and later in the year, though summer afternoons run warm.
wy_second_wind_wall.approach: Follow the walk to the Trailside Wall, then continue up the hill for a couple of minutes to the base.

wy_metropolis.blurb: Metropolis is a sport crag in the upper part of Ten Sleep Canyon, the leftmost of the Mondo Beyondo walls and set between the Downtown and Mondo Beyondo crags. The cliff stands roughly 100 feet. Its lower half is lower-angled and full of cracks, which gives it a handful of moderate pitches that are rare in this canyon, while the upper half steepens into bulges where the harder 5.12 and low 5.13 lines finish. Of the roughly twenty routes here, nearly half fall in the 5.12 range, so it suits climbers who are projecting hard sport more than those warming up. A small boulder with short, steep problems sits below the wall.

wy_nat_s_three_star_roof.blurb: This small bouldering area in Vedauwoo, outside Laramie, sits at about 8,200 feet and is named for a roof crack that is among the longest in the area. Most of the roughly twenty recorded climbs are boulder problems that mix crack and face moves, with a few trad leads and a single bolted line alongside. Grades on the boulders run mainly from V1 to V7, with a couple of far harder problems. The cracks here are the flared, jamming style Vedauwoo is known for, so it rewards climbers who like wide, awkward technique. It makes a quick stop if you are already working the nearby Party Dome.

wy_party_dome.blurb: Party Dome is a rock formation at Vedauwoo near Laramie, the first sizable outcrop on your right as you drive in and just east of the Nat's Three Star Roof area. Roughly twenty climbs are recorded, split between trad leads and boulder problems, with a couple of bolted lines as well. Roped climbs run from beginner-friendly 5.3 and 5.6 up to 5.11, and the boulders reach from V3 up to a few well into the double digits. The walk from the road is short and open, and it tends to be quieter than the bigger Vedauwoo bouldering zones, so it suits a mixed party with both ropes and pads.

wy_g_cowboy_poetry.blurb: Cowboy Poetry is the far east end of the Main Wall at Wild Iris, near Lander, at about 8,700 feet. It is taller than most walls up here, with a vertical to slightly overhanging lower tier of 60 to 70 feet and a steep bulge above. Around twenty-one sport routes are recorded, from a few very easy lines to 5.12. The easier 5.10 and 5.11 routes end at the lower anchors, while the longer, more sustained extensions climb through the bulge. Sun reaches the cliff nearly all day. The trail from the parking lot heads right and downhill for about half a mile to the base.
wy_g_cowboy_poetry.approach: From the parking lot take the first trail on the right, which drops downhill for about half a mile to the base of the cliff.

wy_f_rode_hard_wall.blurb: Rode Hard Wall is a south-facing sport wall on the Main Wall at Wild Iris, near Lander, at about 8,800 feet. It is smaller and cozier than its neighbor Cowboy Poetry, a few hundred feet to the east. A dense forest at the base, a big overhead roof and the concave shape of the cliff make it shadier and breezier than the surrounding walls. The rock changes along its length from smooth white stone to featured, cracked rock to a pocketed slab. Twenty sport routes plus one boulder problem run from 5.9 to 5.13, with the largest groups at 5.11 and 5.12, from juggy slabs to powerful roof climbing.

_conflicts.wy_school_the: Stored rock limestone; the crag page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/113203956/the-school) calls it dolomite. Blurb avoids naming rock.
_conflicts.wy_party_dome: Stored rock granite; one page (https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/conquer-the-party-dome-vedauwoos-first-bold-boulder-formations) says sandstone, the other page names no rock. Left unchanged.
